pipeline_findings.finding: Interchange skeletal import silently drops a clip whose duration is not a whole frame at 30 fps
pipeline_findings.encoded_in: ArtSource/tools/ebs_skelkit.py (ebs-skelkit-v2): write_skinned_glb refuses unaligned clips; frame_aligned_duration()/retime_clip() snap them
pipeline_findings.cost_before_it_was_found: one clip lost in each of EBS-MER-UNT-002, -003 (two) and -004

pipeline_findings.finding: A LOD1 source file carrying collision meshes silently inflates the imported LOD1 triangle count
pipeline_findings.detail: StaticMeshEditorSubsystem.import_lod does not honour UBX_ collision naming the way the primary Interchange import does. A LOD1 glTF that includes the UBX boxes imports them as ordinary render geometry inside the LOD1 sections. On EBS-KHA-BLD-001 that added 24 phantom triangles (634 exported, 658 imported) and the import still reported success apart from the triangle-count check.
pipeline_findings.evidence: /Volumes/Seagate Game Archive/EchoesOfTheBrokenSun/BuildArtifacts/Evidence/asset-production-20260906T221157Z/EBS-KHA-BLD-001/import/ (run1 mismatched at 658, run2 clean at 634)
pipeline_findings.resolution: Write collision into the LOD0 file only: write_glb(..., include_collision=(lod == 0)). Every other generator in this pipeline already did; the Hearth generator did not, so this was my bug, not an engine defect. The import job's lod1_triangles_match check is what caught it.

pipeline_findings.finding: ebs_skelkit pose rotations are (pitch, yaw, roll), and a limb fold written into the yaw slot silently swings the limb sideways
pipeline_findings.detail: On EBS-KHA-UNT-002 every leg stride, body pitch and caster pitch was authored into index 1 (yaw) instead of index 0 (pitch). Nothing errors: the clips build, import and play, and the legs simply swing sideways instead of stepping. It was only visible in a rendered pose.
pipeline_findings.resolution: Corrected in the generator and guarded by a test that requires a stride to be pure pitch with zero yaw and roll. Worth checking in every future creature generator before the first render.
pipeline_findings.related: The same package found that bone heads must sit at the PROXIMAL end of each segment; heads at the distal end make a limb pivot about its far joint and tear away from the body under rotation.

pipeline_findings.finding: A gait whose key time and swing phase are derived from the same value gives every limb an identical curve
pipeline_findings.detail: Both quadruped generators wrote `t = (phase + step) * duration` and `swing = sin(2*pi*(phase + step))`. Because the key time IS the phase argument, each limb received the same set of (time, value) pairs and all four legs moved in unison. The Riftstalker shipped in commit 000e99d with a hop instead of a diagonal gait. Nothing errors, the clips import and play, and it is invisible unless the limbs are compared to each other.
pipeline_findings.resolution: The key time now walks the cycle and the swing is read at that time PLUS the limb's phase. Both generators fixed; the Riftstalker rebuilt, re-tested and re-imported. The Cairnback carries a test that samples each limb's swing and requires four distinct phases, which is what caught it.
pipeline_findings.found_by: writing the Cairnback's gait-separation test, which asserted the two animals walk differently

pipeline_findings.finding: AnimationClip.key APPENDS, so a second key at the same time is never read
pipeline_findings.detail: The sampler takes the first key matching a time. A correction pass that adds a key at an existing time therefore does nothing at all, while looking as though it worked. This silently defeated two rounds of foot-planting corrections on EBS-KHA-UNT-003.
pipeline_findings.resolution: Replace keys by time rather than appending. The Cairnback generator carries a set_key helper that does this.

pipeline_findings.finding: AnimationClip.key appends AND SORTS, so a key-replacement helper that takes the last element deletes the key it meant to insert
pipeline_findings.detail: A helper written to replace a key at an existing time appended the new key, then rebuilt the track from keys[:-1] plus keys[-1], assuming the appended key was last. It is only last when its time is the largest in the track. For every other time the real new key was dropped, which emptied a body track down to one key and made a collapse interpolate from a constant. Nothing errors.
pipeline_findings.resolution: Rebuild the track directly: filter out any key at that time and append a Keyframe, then sort. Fixed in both EBS-KHA-UNT-003 and EBS-KHA-UNT-004, which shared the helper.
pipeline_findings.related: The third silent animation defect in this roster, after the gait phase collapse and the pitch/yaw slot mix-up.

pipeline_findings.finding: Three of eight Kharuun cards described the wrong anatomy because the cards were written before the concepts were traced
pipeline_findings.detail: The Riftstalker was specified as a biped, the Growth Basin's niches as closing, and the Resonant as a biped. All three were contradicted by their own candidates. Every one was corrected against the concept rather than the model being bent to fit the card.
pipeline_findings.resolution: A faction rule now requires a card to be authored AFTER its candidate is traced. The rule arrived three errors late; any future faction's cards are to follow it from the start.

pipeline_findings.finding: I reported that no Kharuun asset card existed. One does, and it governs the Riftstalker.
pipeline_findings.detail: REL-ART-005.KA.RIFTSTALKER is present in Docs/Requirements.md section 18.2's neighbourhood at line 4535, in a second block of asset cards well below the Meridian set I had checked. My claim of 'no Kharuun asset card' was based on searching only the first block. The owner's ruling of 2026-09-07 to author a provisional Kharuun card set was given on that false premise.
pipeline_findings.impact: The Riftstalker was built against my provisional bounds instead of the authoritative card. Triangles and emissive are within the real card, but its three required socket names were absent, its 14-bone rig conflicts with the built 22-bone quadruped, and its three vertex ID channels for molt phases are unimplemented. The other seven Kharuun packages are genuinely uncovered, so the rest of the provisional set stands.
pipeline_findings.resolution: A full audit now enumerates every '#### [Asset Card: ...]' heading and matches it against all 21 packages; the result is recorded in kharuun-asset-cards.json under card_coverage_audit. The Riftstalker emits the card's socket names with its own as aliases, its manifest carries a clause-by-clause compliance table, and the bone-count conflict is raised as OWNER-QUESTION A. Run that audit before claiming a card is absent.

audit_result.note: REL-FAC-027.HC.INTERVALIST is the Intervalist UNIT and does not govern the Interval Loom building.

pipeline_findings.finding: An emissive ceiling measured by surface area can be breached by a STATE, not by the rest pose. The Chorus Loom's producing state measured 6.8% magenta and its researching state 15.4%, because that state doubles the warp. Thinning every thread was the wrong fix: at a 1.0 cm radius the worst state still reached 11.85%, with no headroom and a thinner warp in every state. Making the state's ADDED rows finer than the base rows, and narrowing the beam's lit underside from a 72 cm panel to a 14 cm line, brought it to 10.9% without touching the base read.
pipeline_findings.rule: Measure the emissive ceiling in every state, not the rest pose, and fix a state's breach in what that state adds.

pipeline_findings.finding: ue_import_inspect_skeletal.py reads its job path from the EBS_IMPORT_JOB environment variable. Passing the path as an argument after the script name in -ExecutePythonScript crashed the editor with KeyError: 'EBS_IMPORT_JOB' under -ScriptErrorsAreFatal, and the wrapper log showed only a shutdown handler; the cause was visible solely in the engine's own EBSPreview.log.
pipeline_findings.rule: Set EBS_IMPORT_JOB in the environment, and read the engine log rather than the wrapper log when a headless run exits non-zero. My invocation error, not an engine defect.

pipeline_findings.finding: Collision in a skinned GLB is imported by Interchange as a SECOND SkeletalMesh with its own skeleton. The Phase Anchor was written with include_collision=(lod == 0), copied from an older static-mesh generator; the LOD0 file's UBX box arrived as UBX_SK_EBS_HOL_BLD_004_01 alongside a SK_..._scene_Skeleton, and the inspection failed on 7 imported objects against an expected 5.
pipeline_findings.rule: Skeletal packages in this pipeline export with include_collision=False; collision for a skeletal mesh comes from a physics asset, not from UBX geometry. My deviation from the established convention, not a new engine defect, but the import behaviour is worth knowing.
pipeline_findings.regression_check: ue_import_inspect_skeletal.py fails any import producing a UBX_/UCX_/USP_/UCP_ SkeletalMesh, or more Skeleton assets than the job declares, and names the cause rather than only reporting a count mismatch. Pipeline-wide, verified clean on EBS-HOL-BLD-003 and EBS-HOL-BLD-004. Owner ruling 2026-09-07.

pipeline_findings.finding: Two silent framing traps cost a render cycle each. A radial detail placed at a polygon's VERTEX angle instead of its face centre straddles an edge and never shows on a flat face; and ebs_render's perspective_camera puts the camera at target - arm * forward, so yaw 0 looks at the -X side of a subject, not at its +X face.
pipeline_findings.rule: Place face detail at the apothem and at a face-centre angle, and read perspective_camera before choosing a yaw, rather than inferring the camera's side from a render that shows nothing.

pipeline_findings.finding: Interchange stores skeletal vertex colours as 8-bit unsigned normalised. A glTF round-trip out of Unreal returns componentType 5121, so an authored 0.85 comes back as 0.851 and 0.15 as 0.149.
pipeline_findings.rule: Compare imported vertex colours to the authored values within 1/255, not exactly, and never design a channel that needs more than 256 levels.

pipeline_findings.finding: USkeletalMesh exposes has_vertex_colors() but no Python accessor for the VALUES in 5.8, and MeshDescription offers no per-vertex-instance colour getter either. A flag that says 'colours exist' cannot show that the authored mapping survived.
pipeline_findings.rule: Verify imported vertex data by exporting the asset back out with GLTFSkeletalMeshExporter and reading the attribute as values. Presence is not verification.

pipeline_findings.finding: SkeletalMaterial entries returned by mesh.get_editor_property('materials') are COPIES. Mutating them in place and saving reports success while the asset keeps its old material, which read as a passing assignment until the result was read back.
pipeline_findings.rule: Rebuild the whole materials array and set it as one property, then read it back to confirm.

pipeline_findings.finding: A material authored in a -nullrhi editor has no platform shader map, and loading it in a later rendering run leaves it compiling indefinitely: every captured frame renders the DEFAULT material. It looks exactly like a working assignment - get_material returns the right instance, the parameter reads back, no error is logged. A 90-second pixel-gated wait never went bright; the same material built inside the rendering run was ready on the first poll.
pipeline_findings.rule: Build or recompile a material in the SAME run that renders it, and gate captures on PIXELS rather than on a sleep: sample the render target until it shows the expected response, and fail if it never does.

pipeline_findings.finding: create_dynamic_material_instance reported correctly through get_material but the captures showed the default material. Switching to a MaterialInstanceConstant per parameter value assigned with set_material worked. Both that switch and the -nullrhi fix (PF-016) were made before the first good capture, and the MID path was not re-tested afterwards, so PF-016 is the confirmed cause and the MID behaviour is unresolved.
pipeline_findings.rule: Prefer a MaterialInstanceConstant per value for deterministic headless capture, and do not report a MID assignment as working on the strength of get_material alone.

owner_rulings.subject: Qualifications on the vertex-ID report, and the in-engine capture

rulings.ruling: Higher R means earlier treatment: verify the threshold uses that convention. Tick 0 nothing already swept; tick 80 even the R=0 legs complete. Check intermediate boundaries after 8-bit quantisation.
rulings.applied: A REAL DEFECT was found. The first material compared with a strict '>' and wired the A == B branch to zero, so the R = 0 legs NEVER completed at tick 80. It compiled and was assigned, which is exactly why 'compiles and is assigned' was not evidence. Rebuilt as threshold = 1.02 - progress * 1.04 with '>=': tick 0 sweeps 0 of 10 quantised levels, tick 80 sweeps 10 of 10 including R = 0. The ten quantised levels cross at ten distinct progress values, smallest margin 3.92 ticks against a quantisation step worth about 0.3 ticks. Recorded in sweep-boundaries.json and asserted by a test.

rulings.ruling: Matching distinct-colour sets does not establish spatial assignment or unchanged LODs. Verify placement and membership per LOD, or narrow the claim.
rulings.applied: Both. Placement verified spatially: every imported vertex matched to its authored position within 0.06 cm and its colour compared - LOD0 1056/1056 and LOD1 696/696, zero mismatches. And the claim is narrowed: 'LOD generation altered nothing' is WITHDRAWN. Both imported meshes report a single LOD, so no engine reduction chain exists and none was exercised; that is now recorded as untested.
